description:
## Goal

Every user-visible runtime closure carries one typed source denotation identity shared by interp, JIT, and AOT. The identity names the source function or lambda, not a transport specialization, code address, allocation, capture-count schema, rendered label, or canonical string. Repeated construction of the same lambda has the same denotation; distinct lambda occurrences do not. Deep copy and GC preserve it verbatim.

This is semantic runtime data. Rendering may display it, but display is only a consumer. fz-5xp.27 will combine it with the runtime closure environment to answer strict closure comparison and map-key identity.

## Current contradictions

The first closure word is called closure_schema_id and ordinary allocation fills it from SchemaRegistry::closure_env(captured_count). Closure layout and tracing already use the header capture count, so this registry entry is vestigial. Equal capture counts collide, schema registration order changes the value, interp and native render different values, and no GC-stable source denotation is available to runtime comparison.

BackendConstructionWrapper.identity is not the answer: it is a specialized TransportPosition. One source lambda can have several wrappers. Promoting its ordinal or canonical display number would make specialization and packaging order semantic.

A dense rank of closures reachable from one BackendProgram is also not an identity. The shared macro Process can execute multiple BackendPrograms whose closures coexist, and adding one newly reachable earlier-sorting lambda would renumber retained values. The World FunctionId is already the exact interned denotation domain and survives incremental additions. ClosureDenotationId is its typed runtime projection, never a package-local reranking.

Generated functions are currently keyed by owner plus Span plus arity. Repeated metadata-identical macro expansions and multiple Span::DUMMY lambdas can collapse. The first replacement, a lowered ValueId, is also wrong: with lowers the same else AST once per failing binding, so one source lambda receives several fresh lowered values and several identities. Identity belongs to final source syntax before lowering duplicates it.

Types::ClauseOrder currently uses CallableLabels, a FunctionId to rendered-string map populated by canon::function_label, as production type ordering authority. This violates the same rule at the source. Type ordering and later runtime term ordering must consume a shared immutable typed denotation key; rendering consumes that key separately.

## Strategy

- Introduce one immutable typed function denotation or order key shared by FunctionMap and the Types callable-order projection. Named origin retains typed module origin, source identifier, and arity. Generated origin retains only the owner denotation, typed source occurrence, and arity. Diagnostic spans remain separate source-location data and never participate in identity. Canonical and display code read the typed denotation data.
- Delete CallableLabels, canon::function_label parsing, generated-name encoding, and parse_generated_name. Source identifier strings remain legitimate source data; a formatted display string is never a comparator.
- Assign each lambda a typed structural occurrence once during final quoted-function decoding, in the existing recursive decode traversal. Preserve it in the immutable lambda AST through clones and lowering. Mint GeneratedFunctionKey from owner plus this occurrence plus arity. Do not use Span, heap address, lowered ValueId, a second numbering pass, or a fallback counter during lowering.
- Define ClosureDenotationId as the runtime projection of World FunctionId. Preserve the World-global raw identity across every BackendProgram executed in that World; do not sort or densify reachable subsets.
- Store the denotation in the existing first closure word and rename its accessors accordingly. The execution code word remains a separate concern.
- Thread the denotation through every user closure mint, including zero-capture fn refs, construction wrappers, interpreter materialization, JIT/AOT emission, and static closures.
- Preserve it through Cheney copying and cross-heap deep copy.
- Give scheduler and internal continuation scaffolding an explicit typed sentinel and prove it cannot reach user comparison or rendering.
- Delete ClosureEnv schema registration, capture-count identity comments, ModuleMap::define_anonymous if its zero-callsite census remains true, and duplicate translation data made obsolete by the cutover.

## Signal

- Two allocations of one lambda carry one denotation on every door; two different lambdas with the same arity, capture count, provider metadata span, or Span::DUMMY carry different denotations.
- Reaching one lambda in a with else block through different failed bindings carries one denotation, not one per lowering copy.
- One lambda compiled through multiple activation or callable-wrapper specializations still carries one denotation.
- Adding a later function or executing another BackendProgram in the same World does not renumber a retained denotation.
- Sending a closure and forcing GC preserve the denotation exactly.
- Closure rendering agrees on interp, JIT, and AOT, but no semantic test obtains identity by parsing that rendering.
- Repeated macro expansion creates distinct generated FunctionIds at distinct final-source occurrences while retries of unchanged decoding and lowering reuse the same ids.
- Callable clause order is unchanged under FunctionId mint-order permutations because it asks typed denotations, not labels or raw ids.
- Removing ClosureEnv0 may renumber real struct schemas. Interp, JIT, and AOT must agree after the cutover and behavior or canonical artifacts must remain equivalent; do not reserve a dummy schema merely to preserve obsolete numeric ids.

## TDD and gates

Begin with red tests at source-occurrence decoding, FunctionId minting, callable clause ordering, allocation, multi-program execution, three-door, deep-copy, and GC boundaries. Include metadata-identical macro expansion, Span::DUMMY, with-else lowering duplication, cross-specialization, and a shared Process running successive BackendPrograms. Update semantic-authority, any-value, pipeline, macro-expansion, type-world, and canonical-form documentation. Full lib, runtime, fixture, CLI, AOT integration, fmt, and warnings-denied clippy gates plus a fresh ticket-scoped cold review precede one commit and close.

comments.text: fz-kdt.209 (filed 2026-09-03) is the sibling of this ticket on the GATE side: test gates assert types by display() output, which is non-injective (fz-go4.34 recorded arrow display collisions; fz-kdt.183 recorded list/non_empty_list collapse). Same root idea as yours -- a rendering is not an identity.

title: Give every runtime closure one typed source denotation; delete ClosureEnv schema identity
